items.title: [Remoto] Desenvolvedor Java Pleno - DB1/ANYMARKET
items.description:
<!-- Por favor, poste apenas vagas para backend. -->

## Nossa empresa

Na DB1, cada linha de código, teste ou insight é uma chance de criar impacto real. Somos movidos pela curiosidade e pelo desejo de transformar problemas complexos em soluções que simplificam a vida das pessoas. Gostamos de experimentar, aprender e inovar, e por isso esse é o lugar para colocar seu talento à prova.

Se você combina inteligência com uma vontade incansável de aprender e evoluir, e tem uma postura resiliente moldado por superações, já carrega muito da essência DB1. Aqui, cada desafio é oportunidade de crescimento, cada erro é uma lição para voltar mais forte e cada vitória é combustível para seguir adiante com uma missão clara e valores sólidos que dão sentido a cada passo. Na DB1, superação não é exceção e sim parte da jornada.

## Descrição da vaga

No Anymarket, você vai construir o coração das nossas integrações, sistemas robustos, escaláveis e que atravessam times diferentes, do backend ao frontend. Sua missão começa pela imersão: entender o que existe, como funciona e por quê foi construído assim. A partir daí, você vai ganhar autonomia para evoluir essas soluções e habilitar a escala que o produto precisa para crescer.

No dia a dia, você vai trabalhar com times multidisciplinares de tecnologia, negócio e design, sempre com IA como aliada no fluxo de desenvolvimento, geração e revisão de código, análise de logs, automação de tarefas e spec-driven development fazem parte da rotina. Você vai escrever código que resiste ao tempo, do tipo que nasce forte desde o primeiro commit e continua de pé anos depois.

## Local

Remoto

## Requisitos

Perfil que buscamos:

- Experiência sólida em Java com Spring Boot e/ou Quarkus, não só domínio do framework, mas entendimento do que acontece por trás dele
- Experiência com PostgreSQL ou banco relacional equivalente
- Vivência com Redis ou similar para caching
- Experiência com mensageria assíncrona: Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ ou similar
- Conhecimento do ciclo completo de deploy: Docker, Kubernetes e CI/CD
- Vivência real com arquitetura de microsserviços
- Experiência com monitoramento em tempo real: Datadog, Grafana, ELK ou similar
- IA incorporada ao fluxo de trabalho: geração e revisão de código, RAG, spec-driven development (SDD)
- Quando trava num problema, busca ativamente a solução, questiona colegas, pesquisa, decompõe em partes menores
- Assume responsabilidade pelos próprios erros e colabora genuinamente em equipe

Vai ser incrível se você souber ou tiver vontade de aprender:

- MongoDB ou outro banco não-relacional
- AWS em nível intermediário
- Análise de performance em produção
- Ferramentas de análise estática de código (Sonar/SAST)
- Fluxos de autenticação OAuth2/PKCE 

## Benefícios

Cartão de benefícios flexíveis (Alimentação, Mobilidade, Qualidade de Vida, entre outras categorias);
Plano de Saúde Unimed;
Seguro de Vida;
Plano odontológico (opcional);
Crédito Consignado com as melhores taxas (Mixtra);
Gift Aniversário;
Bem-estar: parceria com plataforma de acesso a academias e outras atividades físicas, parceria para atendimento psicológico;
Evolução de carreira: Parceria com plataformas e instituições de ensino, tanto para idiomas quanto para graduação, pós-graduação e cursos livres, Plano de Desenvolvimento Individual (PDI), feedbacks constantes, Programa de Mentoria, eventos internos, subsídio para treinamentos, universidade corporativa e muito mais;
Programas de recompensa: bônus para indicação de novos colaboradores e bônus anual atrelado a metas;
Espaço para assumir desafios e se desenvolver.

## Contratação

CLT

items.title: 9 company profiles whose domains no longer exist
items.description:
While checking careers links across `src/companies/` (2026-10-11), I found profiles whose company website and careers page are both unreachable. For these 9, the domain no longer resolves at all (NXDOMAIN, checked twice), so the company looks closed or renamed:

| Profile | Website |
|---|---|
| Cuvette | https://cuvette.tech |
| GitPrime | https://gitprime.com/ (acquired by Pluralsight in 2019) |
| Grou.ps | https://build.gr.ps |
| Impira | https://www.impira.com/ |
| Mobile Jazz | https://mobilejazz.com |
| Park Assist | https://tech.parkassist.com |
| Pathable | https://pathable.com/ |
| Socket Supply Co | https://socketsupply.co |
| Telestax Inc. | https://telestax.com/ |

Related:
- **Interactive Intelligence**: `inin.com` now redirects to Genesys, which acquired it.
- **Bugfender**: its `careers_url` is `https://mobilejazz.com/jobs`, on the dead Mobile Jazz domain above.

CONTRIBUTING says profiles are normally removed when a company no longer meets the criteria, so I didn't want to delete these without asking. Happy to open a PR removing them (and fixing Bugfender's link) if you agree.

(Separately, #2270 updates 9 careers links that moved.)

items.title: [Bug]: Workday tenants that null locationsText publish out-of-region jobs and lose JobPosting JSON-LD
items.description:
### Bug Type

Scraper: incorrect job information (title, location, date)

### Description

The Workday adapter drops the location for tenants whose search payload returns `locationsText: null`, so those postings publish with an **empty location**. Two concrete consequences:

**1. The target-country gate is bypassed, and out-of-region jobs reach the curated board.**

`scripts/ngj/locations.py` deliberately treats an empty location as *unknown, not foreign* (module docstring, lines 18–21). That is correct for sources that genuinely omit locations — but these tenants do not omit it, the adapter simply never reads it. The location is still present, encoded in `externalPath` as the `/job/<Location>/` segment.

Result on the current published run: **90 curated jobs sit in Warsaw, Manila, Paris, Singapore, Prague, Lisbon, Stockholm, Riga, Blagnac, Torino, Kronberg, Bratislava and more** — 53 distinct non-target locations — on a board that advertises itself as US/Canada/India only. The filter that should have caught them ran against `""` and passed.

**2. 391 jobs lose their JobPosting structured data.**

`site/scripts/seo/jobposting.mjs:122` refuses to emit markup it cannot fill honestly:

```js
const location = locationProps(job.location);
if (!location) return { posting: null, reason: 'unresolvable location' };
```

Those pages still build and still appear in the sitemap, but carry no `JobPosting` JSON-LD, so they are effectively invisible to Google Jobs. **363 of 2877 curated jobs (12.6%) display an em-dash** for location (`site/src/lib/jobs.js:117`, `loc: raw.location || '—'`) and cannot be filtered by location.

All 363 affected jobs are Accenture. The other 1056 Workday jobs parse correctly, so the bug is tenant-shape-specific.

**Affected code** — `scripts/ngj/sources/workday.py:189`:

```python
'location': item.get('locationsText') or '',
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fetch Accenture from its Workday tenant (`https://accenture.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/AccentureCareers`). Confirmed live — the payload returns **both** location fields null while the URL still carries the city:

   ```json
   {
     "title": "Software Engineering New Associate (Fresh Diploma Graduate Program)",
     "locationsText": null,
     "postedLocations": null,
     "externalPath": "/job/Singapore/Software-Engineering-New-Associate--Fresh-Diploma-Graduate-Program-_R00144534"
   }
   ```

2. Run a scrape with `NGJ_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/ngj make run`.
3. Inspect `site/public/jobs.json`: 363 Workday jobs have `location: ""`.
4. Parse the `/job/<segment>/` out of each job's `url` — 53 distinct segments fail `is_valid_location()`; 90 jobs are out of region.
5. Run `npm run build` — the SEO plugin reports `2486 with JobPosting JSON-LD; skipped — unresolvable location: 391`.
6. Open any affected job page: no `JobPosting` JSON-LD in the source, and the board shows `—` where the location should be.

### Suggested Fix

Read the `/job/<Location>/` segment from `externalPath` as a fallback in `_to_job` (`scripts/ngj/sources/workday.py`):

```python
def _location_from_path(item: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    if item.get('locationsText'):
        return item['locationsText']
    match = re.match(r'^/job/([^/]+)/', item.get('externalPath') or '')
    return match.group(1).replace('-', ' ') if match else ''
```

This makes the 90 out-of-region jobs correctly fail the location gate, restores JSON-LD for the rest, and removes the em-dashes.

### Additional Context

**Regression tests worth adding** (both would have caught this the day the tenant's payload shape changed, and guard the next tenant that does the same):

- A Workday item with `locationsText: null` still yields a location derived from `externalPath`.
- A posting whose location resolves to a non-target country never reaches `jobs.json`.

**Verification performed**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest` | 1566 passed, 96.1% coverage |
| `vitest` | 450 passed |
| Playwright E2E + axe | 75 passed |
| `ruff` / `mypy` / `eslint` / `actionlint` | clean |
| `check_integrity.py` on current data | `status: ok`, 0 errors |
| Build with `site/public/` removed | builds clean |

This is a data-correctness bug, not a regression in the existing suites — no current test exercises a Workday tenant that nulls `locationsText`.

**Related, not the same issue:** #243 covers inconsistent *documentation* wording about US vs CA/IN scope. This issue is about the location *gate* being bypassed at runtime by postings that should have been excluded.

**Note on `/job/<Location>/` edge cases:** some segments are building-qualified rather than a clean city (e.g. `Warsaw-Sienna-39`, `Kronberg-Campus-Kronberg-1`, `Kuala-Lumpur-Vertical-Corp-Tower-B`). These still fail the gate correctly, so the fix is safe without a full place-name parser — but a follow-up cleanup for tidier display would be reasonable.

items.title: Add an "Updated At" timestamp column so readers can spot new roles
items.description:
The `Date Posted` column is day-level only, so when new roles get added between refreshes there's no way to tell which rows are new since my last visit — I have to re-scan the whole table from the top and remember where I left off.

Proposal: add a column (e.g. `Updated At`) showing the date + time each row was added or updated by the bot, like:

| Company | Job Title | Location | Date Posted | Updated At |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Company A | ... | ... | Sep 29 | Sep 29, 13:53 |
| Company B | ... | ... | Sep 29 | Sep 29, 17:54 |

This should be feasible since the bot already knows when it inserts each row (the timestamp is implicit in the commit history today) — persisting it per-row just makes it visible to everyone. Readers could then instantly see what's new since their last refresh.

# Security Engineer

**Sen Works Viet Nam Co., Ltd.**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Job Title** | Security Engineer |
| **Department** | IT Services – Information Security |
| **Reports To** | Head of Information Security / Client Security Lead [to be confirmed] |
| **Employment Type** | Full-time labour contract with Sen Works Viet Nam Co., Ltd.; probation of up to 60 days |
| **Work Location** | Vietnam – fully remote |
| **Salary Range** | Up to USD3200 gross/month |

📩 **Apply:** send your CV to [jobs@senworks.com](mailto:jobs@senworks.com)

---

## About Sen Works Viet Nam

Sen Works Viet Nam Co., Ltd. is a Vietnam-based technology and healthcare operations company delivering software development, IT services and revenue cycle management support to healthcare organisations in the United States and Europe. Our people work as dedicated, long-term members of our clients' teams, operating within each client's environment, tools and security standards.

## Role Summary

In this role you will be dedicated to a US healthcare services client that operates a growing network of affiliated medical practices. You will work inside the client's Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 environment and collaborate daily with the client's US-based teams on systems that store, process or transmit protected health information (PHI).

The Security Engineer is the primary architect and engineer of preventive and detective security controls across the client's endpoint, identity, network, cloud and application layers. You will lead the design, implementation and continuous improvement of the security control environment, run vulnerability management, and build the technical evidence that keeps the client audit-ready.

## Key Responsibilities

### Security Architecture & Engineering

- Design, deploy and manage core security platforms: EDR, email security, identity protection, privileged access management, network security and data loss prevention.
- Advance zero trust across identity, device, network and application layers, strengthening conditional access, MFA and least privilege.
- Improve Azure and Microsoft 365 security posture through configuration baselines, policy as code and continuous posture management.
- Set security standards, hardening baselines and reference architectures; run security design reviews for new systems, integrations, vendors and changes.

### Vulnerability & Threat Management

- Lead the vulnerability management program: scanning coverage, risk-based prioritisation, remediation tracking and exception governance.
- Align patching, configuration and end-of-life remediation with security priorities and clinical uptime requirements.
- Direct penetration tests, red team engagements and attack surface management, and validate remediation.
- Use threat intelligence and healthcare-sector attack trends to refine control priorities.

### Compliance Engineering & Detection Enablement

- Build technical controls and evidence supporting HIPAA Security Rule, HITRUST, SOC 2 and client security requirements.
- Strengthen SOC detection by engineering log sources, telemetry pipelines and automated response integrations.
- Define measures for control coverage, vulnerability remediation and platform health; report control gaps, risk posture and investment priorities to leadership.
- Manage security vendors, MSPs and consultants.

### Education & Certifications

- Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems or a related field; an equivalent combination of education, certifications and experience will be considered.
- **CISSP, CCSP** or equivalent advanced security certification required; Microsoft SC-100 or AZ-500 preferred.

### Experience

- 7+ years of information security experience, including at least 3 years in security engineering or architecture.
- Experience designing and operating enterprise security platforms across endpoint, identity, email, network and cloud.
- Proven success measurably reducing risk, e.g. remediation rates, MFA and EDR coverage, or reduced privileged access.
- Experience supporting HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 or ISO 27001 assessments with technical evidence and remediation.
- Healthcare, healthcare technology or managed services experience is a strong advantage.

### Knowledge & Skills

- Security controls in Azure, Microsoft 365 and hybrid Active Directory environments.
- NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, CIS Controls and zero trust principles.
- IAM, PKI, network segmentation, encryption and secure configuration management.
- EDR, SIEM, SOAR, PAM, DLP, email security, vulnerability scanning and CSPM platforms.
- PowerShell, Python and infrastructure as code for automation and evidence collection.
- HIPAA Security Rule and HITRUST CSF control mapping (training provided).
- Professional English (spoken and written) for daily work with US-based colleagues and clients.

### Personal Abilities

- Design controls that reduce risk without impeding clinical workflows.
- Translate emerging threats into practical control improvements and lead implementations through to handoff.
- Present risk and architecture decisions clearly in English to executive and clinical leadership.

## Working Conditions

- Flexible working hours, with an agreed daily overlap window with US-based teams for meetings and real-time collaboration; participation in a shared on-call escalation rotation for security incidents.
- A dedicated, private workspace with stable high-speed internet suitable for handling confidential information and PHI.
- Fully remote from Vietnam.
- Prolonged computer use and extended phone and video communication; sustained concentration during incidents, maintenance windows and time-sensitive work.

## What We Offer

- 💰 Salary reviewed annually.
- 🏠 Flexible working hours and fully remote work.
- 🎁 13th-month salary and performance bonus.
- 🌙 Night-shift allowance in accordance with the Vietnam Labour Code for any additional hours worked at night.
- 🏥 Full social, health and unemployment insurance in accordance with Vietnamese law, plus private healthcare insurance.
- 📚 Company-sponsored certifications and training budget.
- 💻 Company-managed laptop and equipment.
- 🌴 Annual leave of at least 12 days plus Vietnamese public holidays.
- 🌍 Long-term work with international teams on US healthcare technology.

---
